title: Slide design
examples: How do I make sure my slides don't have too much text?
What is the best way to use contrast in a presentation?
Can you show me an example of a slide with only one message?

explain.say: Today we are learning about effective slide design for professional presentations.
Try to dedicate each slide to only one core message for the audience.
For example, if you discuss marketing, one slide should only cover the budget.
Next we will look at using contrast to make your points stand out clearly.
A good contrast example is using dark blue text on a white background.
In real life, think about reading a printed report in bright sunlight.

faq.q: How many points should I put on one slide?
faq.a: It is best to stick to one primary message per slide to keep the audience focused. You might also ask, what is the rule for text per slide? Or, how many ideas fit on one slide?
asks: What is the ideal slide content?

faq.q: What is the best contrast ratio for professional slides?
faq.a: Generally, dark text on a light background provides the clearest contrast for most settings. You could also ask, what colors contrast well? Or, how do I improve readability?
asks: How do I make text pop?
Is black on white always best?

faq.q: Should I use images or just text on my slides?
faq.a: Use visuals to support your single message, rather than letting them replace it entirely. You might also ask, can I use pictures? Or, should I rely on graphics?
asks: How much visual support is okay?

faq.q: If I have many related ideas, how do I structure them?
faq.a: Group related ideas into separate sections, dedicating a main slide to the overarching theme of that section. You could also ask, how do I structure a long talk? Or, should I use section breaks?

faq.q: Does the background color affect the message?
faq.a: Yes, the background color heavily influences readability and the perceived tone of your message. You might ask, what background colors are safe? Or, how does color affect mood?

facts: One core message per slide improves audience retention significantly.
High contrast pairings, like black text on white, maximize readability.
Contrast is the difference between elements, like light and dark.
Visuals should always support, not overwhelm, the main point.

quiz.say: A slide that discusses your company’s sales, marketing, and HR policy all at once violates which rule?

options.show: The slide should focus on only one topic.
options.say: The slide should focus on only one topic.

options.show: Putting a title and three subheadings
options.say: Putting a title and three subheadings

quiz.why: This keeps the audience from feeling overloaded and helps them remember the key takeaway.

wrong.1: This is tempting because it seems organized, but it often leads to too much text.
wrong.2: This seems vibrant, but it actually creates visual chaos and lowers contrast.
wrong.3: This seems structured, but it often forces you to cover too many ideas at once.

quiz.say: If you use yellow text on a pale yellow background, what is the main problem?

options.show: The text will be difficult to read.
options.say: The text will be difficult to read.

options.show: It looks very modern and artistic.
options.say: It looks very modern and artistic.

options.show: It suggests a soft, gentle tone.
options.say: It suggests a soft, gentle tone.

options.show: It matches the overall brand palette.
options.say: It matches the overall brand palette.

quiz.why: Contrast requires a noticeable difference between the foreground and background elements.

wrong.1: This is tempting because it looks trendy, but readability is more important than style here.
wrong.2: This is tempting because it sounds polite, but it sacrifices necessary visual impact.
wrong.3: This is tempting because it looks cohesive, but matching colors can easily result in low contrast.

quiz.say: To ensure your key data point about Q3 growth is noticed, what should you adjust?

options.show: Put a box around the number.
options.say: Put a box around the number.

options.show: Increase the contrast around the Q3 growth number.
options.say: Increase the contrast around the Q3 growth number.

options.show: Make the font size much larger.
options.say: Make the font size much larger.

options.show: Use a bright, neon color for the number.
options.say: Use a bright, neon color for the number.

quiz.why: By increasing contrast, you force the audience's eye directly to the most important piece of information.

wrong.0: This is tempting because it contains the data, but a box alone does not guarantee focus.
wrong.2: This is tempting because it draws attention, but if everything is huge, nothing stands out.
wrong.3: This is tempting because it is bright, but overly bright colors can cause eye strain.
